title: Changing Speed and Direction
seo_title: Kindergarten Speed and Direction Worksheets: Ramps, Walls and Did It Work?
standard_text: Analyze data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with a push or a pull.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten science worksheets on changing speed and direction (NGSS K-PS2-2): ramps, rough and smooth floors, walls that turn a ball and simple tests. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Ramps and floors change speed. Walls change direction.
body_html:
How to think about it

We can change how things move.

  • Speed: steep ramp fast, rough ground slow.
  • Direction: a wall turns a ball.
  • Test it. Did it work?
Example

A ball rolls down a steep ramp. Fast or slow?

Steep is fast.

Answer: fast

Example

A ball hits a wall. What changes?

It bounces a new way.

Answer: its direction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a ball can only go straight.
  • Thinking rough carpet makes a car go faster.
  • Saying a test worked when the ball missed the goal.

faq.q: How can you make a ball go faster?
faq.a: Push it harder or roll it down a steeper ramp.

faq.q: How can you make a ball turn?
faq.a: Put a wall or bumper in its path. The push from the wall changes its direction.

faq.q: How do you know a design works?
faq.a: Test it and look at the result. Did the ball reach the goal or stop in time?
